custom_logic_notes: Martingale EA: opens a single market order in a fixed or random direction. If the trade reaches a profit target (TakeProfit in money), it closes all and resets lot size. If the trade goes against the position by a distance (Step in points), it opens an additional position in the same direction with a larger lot (Lot * Multiplier). This continues until the aggregate profit across all open positions reaches TakeProfit. No stop loss on individual trades - the strategy relies on averaging down with increasing size, which is inherently high-risk and margin-dependent. The Step parameter controls the distance in points between successive entries. After a winning cycle (all positions closed at profit), lot resets to initial. After a losing cycle (margin call or stop out), the position sizing escalation makes recovery impossible without sufficient margin.
python_conversion_notes: Martingale/grid strategies are extremely difficult to backtest accurately in Python because: (1) Position sizing depends on account equity/margin which changes with every trade, (2) Multiple positions in same direction need to be tracked as a basket with aggregate profit calculation, (3) No individual SL means positions can grow indefinitely - margin call simulation required, (4) The Step parameter creates a grid-like entry pattern that needs persistent order management across many bars, (5) Tick-level entry precision matters for the Step distance calculation. Recommend classifying as mt5_only for accurate backtesting, or implementing a simplified version that simulates the basket-level P&L without full margin modeling.
